messages:
jing: Heads-up — noticed sustained VRAM growth when running long-context chat workloads with paged KV on H100. memory_use keeps climbing even after evict attempts, looks like some pages aren't being reclaimed. attaching short traces below.

oliver: repro? config?

jing: repro steps small: run paged-attn with seq_len=4096, batch=4, longctx=48k tokens, kv_mode=paged, reuse_window=8192. Observed ~6GB growth over 30 min on 80GB H100.

maria: can you paste the eviction logs? also which kernel selection profile?

jing: paste logs:
```
[2025-06-11T14:12:03Z] kvcache: evict_attempt id=0x7f2a count=128 target_free=2GB freed=1.6GB
[2025-06-11T14:12:03Z] kvcache: evict_failed slot=0x3ff reason=pt_unmap_mismatch
[2025-06-11T14:12:15Z] kvcache: pgmap: stale_ref detected page=0xabcde owner_gpu=0 refcount=0
[2025-06-11T14:12:40Z] kvcache: allocator: slab_split->split_count=4 orphaned=2
[2025-06-11T14:13:00Z] runtime: kernel=attn_causal_opt2 selected for seq=256
```

oliver: "pt_unmap_mismatch" / "stale_ref" look like page-table bookkeeping races. did you hit this only on H100?

jing: tried on rtx6000 and MI250X. rtx6000 shows small oscillation but stabilizes; MI250X had faster churn but no leak. H100 is the only one with steady upward trend.

chad: hypothesis: H100 NVLINK/coherency path + kernel ordering yields an evict completion being observed before the GPU page table owner clears its pointer, so our slotmap keeps a phantom reference. basically an ordering gap between device fence and host-side metadata cleanup.

maria: interesting — kernel selection might matter. I see you picked attn_causal_opt2 for shorter seqs in traces; that kernel uses asynchronous async-unmap path (fast free). Could be a missing device->host sync there.

oliver: can you capture a short repro trace with KV_CACHE_DEBUG=1 and ktrace enabled? even a 60s flame with the sequence that grows should show the moment where freed pages don't reduce residency.

jing: attaching a trimmed ktrace snippet below. note: lines grouped by thread: (truncated)
```
TRACE: alloc_page slot=0x27 ref=1 -> map_gpu(gpu0)
TRACE: fill_kv slot=0x27 owner=gpu0 seq=2012
TRACE: evict_attempt slot=0x27 -> unlock
TRACE: device_fence signaled seq=3790
TRACE: host_unmap slot=0x27 -> mark_free
TRACE: reclaim_scan sees slot=0x27 ref=0 but page still mapped on gpu0
TRACE: pt_unmap request queued to device but device replied with stale_owner
```

chad: that "stale_owner" device reply smells like a race where the page got migrated/evicted by another stream but the host-side slot wasn't updated atomically. we had a similar but not-identical pattern with pagefolding.

maria: ping @oliver — can you run the kernel with an extra host-device sync in the unmap path to see if it masks the leak (non-prod patch)? add cudaDeviceSynchronize() after queuing unmap on H100. if growth stops, it's ordering.

oliver: ran quick build -> inserted sync after unmap submit on H100, re-ran 30m. result: memory stabilized, freed ratio ~target. no more pt_unmap_mismatch logs. however throughput dropped ~4-5%.

jing: good signal. so either we add a selective fence for H100 or audit the unmap path for atomicity. selective fence + telemetry could be acceptable for Dedicated until we fix kernel ordering.

maria: we should also test with different kernel selections — maybe opt2 triggers a code path that skips a necessary callback. can you force the fallback kernel (attn_generic) and repeat without the sync?

oliver: forced attn_generic (seq kernel override) without sync on H100: memory growth did not occur. so combinatorial: kernel=opt2 + H100 async unmap => leak.

chad: sounds like opt2 uses a different NVTX/stream attachment and submits unmap to a non-default stream; unmap completion callback may race with host metadata updates. we need to ensure that page-table ownership transfer is observed by the host only after device acks unmap completion. possible fixes: 1) always use event-based callback that does host update on callback; 2) use release-acquire fence semantics when flipping owner bits in slotmap; 3) selective device sync for H100 opt2.

jing: for short-term mitigation I'll push a runtime flag: kvcache.unmap_fence=auto (auto => fence on known hw/kernel combos: H100+opt2). will push PR and CI job to run longctx stress for 1h on H100 pool.

maria: please include compact trace snippet and the minimal repro (we can add to perf-regress job). also record perf counters: TLB misses, pagefaults, cudaStreamWaitSignal counts.

oliver: open PR with draft changelist and test config. note: we should also attempt a non-blocking fix: flip owner using atomic exchange with smp_wmb equivalent in host code before submitting unmap; that might preserve throughput. I'll prototype.

jing: created a short ticket in sprint board: KB-2337 "H100 paged KV: opt2 unmap ordering -> leak". linking traces in the ticket.

sre-bot: deploy/ci started for pr/4921 (kvcache: unmap_fence default auto). buildkite: https://bk.redwood.ai/organizations/redwood/pipelines/kvcache/builds/4921

chad: next steps: oliver prototype atomic-owner flip, maria verify kernel paths that submit unmap on non-default streams, jing run 1h stress on dedicated h100. if all green, roll to dedicated pools and add telemetry metric: evict_mismatch_rate.

maria: also add a regression test that runs opt2 with longctx and asserts resident_pages after eviction <= threshold. small fuzz harness should catch this going forward. :white_check_mark:

jing: thanks all — keeping thread updates here as we have traces. will post PR link + buildkite results when green. :rocket:
